In 2000, two small non-load bearing walls were taken down to provide access via an easement between Condominium Units 4 and 5 at the 30 Hancock Street Condominium.    The deeds of the two units, taxes and utilities remained separate and the condominium is currently and will remain a six-unit condominium. Boston ISD did not change the occupancy of the building at the time.  The deeds of the two units, taxes and utilities are currently and will all continue to remain separate. The proposed project consists of reconstructing the two small non-load bearing walls to re-box in the stairwell between Condominium Units 4 and 5.  The project will also involve moving one electric light switch and alteration to the current fire alarm system to address the fact that Units 4 and 5 will return to completely separate spaces with no easement between them.  Currently, the only utility service that is combined between Units 4 and 5 is the fire/smoke alarm system. All other systems are separate.  Units 4 and 5 currently share a 24 Volt smoke/fire/CO system that all connect to an independent fire alarm control panel on the 5th floor of the building in Unit 5.   In splitting the two unit’s fire alarm systems, Owner’s contractors, Fire Alarm Queen and Lowe Electric will remove the existing 24 volt smoke and fire alarm devices and install new 120 volt devices as shown on the included architect’s stamped drawing.  Fire Alarm Queen will adjust the programing on the building’s existing monitored system to address the changes to the system.  Lowe Electric will perform the electric wiring for the new 120 volt devices.  Within the last 12 Months, 30 Hancock Street upgraded its fire alarm system to comply with the requirements of a 6 unit-building as required by the Boston Fire Department.

The limited work is set forth in the attached plans submitted with this application.  The fire alarm work arose because the current Owner wishes to eliminate the easement and sell Unit 4.  The existing building system was installed by Fire Alarm Queen and Lowe Electric in the last 12 months and there have been no changes in the system since that install.

Eight dome cameras will be located inside the building to watch the exit/entry doors to the equipment storage and tool counter, and also one in each the training and office areas.

Barrier bars will be installed on the basement awning windows.  Two motion detectors will be installed in the home's interior. This comprehensive plumbing project at 300 Commercial St, Unit 304, Boston, MA, encompasses three main components: kitchen sink relocation, bar sink installation, and make-safe demolition work. The kitchen sink scope involves re-routing PVC drain lines and water supply lines while maintaining approximately the same location, with slight adjustments to accommodate the vent piping position into the post. This includes the installation of a new 1/4" water line to the refrigerator from the main kitchen sink cabinet. The finish work comprises mounting a faucet, installing a drain trap, connecting a garbage disposal, and completing both dishwasher and refrigerator hookups.
A new bar sink installation will be added to the space, requiring new PVC drain piping and water supply lines. The plumbing vent for this fixture will extend to the laundry location and tie into the existing vent system. Final tie-in points for both water and drain lines will be determined post-demolition, with potential connection points at either the kitchen sink or laundry location. The bar sink finish work includes mounting the sink and installing a trap with a full-size clean-out for future maintenance.
Prior to the main construction work, a make-safe demolition will be performed on the existing kitchen plumbing. This involves properly disconnecting and capping all water and drain lines, with thorough leak testing to ensure system integrity.
